recentItems.title: The truth behind France's student protests #FourReal #France #Protests #Students #Youth #Politics
recentItems.description:
France’s young people are angry, and their protests are getting increasingly violent.

But what’s driving them onto the streets?

Students are describing overcrowded classrooms, missing teachers and schools struggling to cope. Now, as France faces pressure to cut public spending, they fear they’ll be asked to do more with less.

And the protests are becoming a political battleground, with the government and opposition blaming each other for the violence and what it says about France’s future.

What started as a fight over schools has become a much bigger argument about public services, money and politics, with a presidential election looming. And the students say they’re not stopping.

recentItems.description:

recentItems.description:

recentItems.title: India's Gen Z protesters demand election chief RESIGNS
recentItems.description:
India’s ‘cockroaches’ are back.

This time, the Gen-Z movement is demanding the resignation of the man overseeing the country’s elections - Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar - to resign.

[Subscribe to our Substack newsletter: https://channel4news.substack.com/subscribe]

They claim more than 130 million names have been deleted from India’s electoral roll.

It comes just months after the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) inspired a wave of protests across the country earlier this year, which led to the resignation of India's education minister following an exam leak scandal.

Authorities have said the commission’s so-called Special Intensive Revision is just a draft, to remove duplicates and ineligible entries.

But critics - including opposition leader Rahul Gandhi - have warned that it’s a way of manipulating the voting system in favour of Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

Mr Gandhi was detained by police this after he joined dozens of other MPs in marching on the Election Commission’s headquarters, as protests have erupted across Delhi and Mumbai in the wake of the controversy.

More demonstrations have been organised on October 8 and October 10.

Mr Kumar hasn’t commented on the issue, but the commission and Modi's ruling Bharatiya Janata Party denied the accusations.

In this episode of the breakdown, we explore if this really was an attempt to clean up India’s electoral roll, or whether millions of legitimate voters could be shut out.

We speak to Uday Chandra, Professor in Comparative Politics and International Relations at Ashoka University in India, and ask whether a youth movement that brought down one minister, could now take on the officials running the world’s biggest democracy.

recentItems.title: What next for Christa Pike as death row inmate WAKES UP after two lethal injections
recentItems.description:
The unprecedented survival of Christa Pike following a botched lethal injection in Tennessee has plunged the American capital punishment system into a deep legal and constitutional crisis. 

WARNING: This episode discusses issues some viewers may find distressing

[Subscribe to our Substack newsletter: https://channel4news.substack.com/subscribe]

Sentenced to death at age 18 for the 1995 murder of Colleen Slemmer, Pike was scheduled to become the first woman executed by the state in over two centuries. However, after two lethal doses of pentobarbital failed to kill her, she survived and was rushed to intensive care.

Pike is now reportedly conscious and speaking in hospital while handcuffed to her bed.

In this episode of The Fourcast, Anushka Asthana is joined by Dr. Joel Zivot, an anaesthesiologist advising Pike's defence team,  Robin Maher from the Death Penalty Information Center, and "Surviving Execution" author Ian Woods. The panel asks: Can an execution ever truly be humane, or has America reached a breaking point with capital punishment?

recentItems.title: Zelenskyy condemns ‘vile’ Russian strikes after Ukraine cities pounded
recentItems.description:
Russian missiles have pounded cities across Ukraine in what President Zelenskyy described as “vile strikes” on his country. At least 24 people have been killed. Russia said it carried out a 'massive strike' targeting military and industrial facilities using high precision land, sea and air launched weapons.  

[Subscribe to our Substack newsletter: https://channel4news.substack.com/subscribe]

And Vladimir Putin’s reportedly favourite Russian resort of Sochi, on the Black Sea, was blanketed in black smoke after a nearby oil tanker was struck by a naval drone.

recentItems.title: Reform UK clears itself of wrongdoing after undercover investigation
recentItems.description:
Reform UK has today published its internal report into allegations that senior figures in the party breached the law on party donations.

It relates to an undercover investigation - that included meetings with leader Nigel Farage - broadcast last month by this programme and Verbatim, a group of journalists from the Centre for Climate reporting. Their footage and findings were verified by us.

[Subscribe to our Substack newsletter: https://channel4news.substack.com/subscribe]

Today, Reform UK report says there was no law breaking. Labour said "you can find more whitewash in this report than at your local B&Q."

The Metropolitan Police is carrying out its own criminal inquiry into the findings of the undercover investigation.
